621c679bb61c: A · Vectors, dot products, and length: calculating with a list of numbers
596260646b8c: Think of a vector as a column of numbers. Position (3,4) means 3 right and 4 up; addition works entry by entry. Bold symbols denote the whole column, ordinary letters a single number. A dot product multiplies matching entries and sums them. Pythagoras gives the length. Transpose T turns a column into a row without changing its values.
cc569e2d7614: Here, “normalize” means divide by length to obtain length 1, not make every coordinate 1. A zero denominator has no direction and cannot be normalized. An outer product instead keeps every pairwise product in a table:
70213c053bd5: The ∑ symbol adds all terms in the specified range; ∏ multiplies them all.
ffd2c0bc1631: B · Matrices: a table of linear equations
1fa9f66cf89d: Multiplying a matrix by a column vector takes one dot product per row. A 2×3 matrix has 2 rows and 3 columns, turning 3 inputs into 2 outputs. AB means apply B first, then A; the order generally cannot be swapped.
02842d0c05dc: I is the identity matrix: it returns the input unchanged. An inverse undoes a transformation. An irreversible transformation, such as collapsing a dimension to zero, has no inverse. A rotation preserves length, so its inverse is its transpose. diag puts numbers on the diagonal and zeros elsewhere.
b9dbd8d331db: C · Exponentials and logarithms: from repeated multiplication to continuous growth
061f3c0330f0: 2³ multiplies three copies of 2; 2⁻³ is its reciprocal; 2^(1/2) is √2. Subdividing exponents more finely extends the definition to real numbers. e≈2.71828 is a special base whose rate of growth equals its own value. ln reverses exponentiation; a calculator can evaluate it.
de042e96e8a2: An exponential is always positive. A negative square in the exponent makes the value approach zero as its input moves away from zero, giving the Gaussian shape. ln is increasing on positive numbers, so taking ln on both sides preserves an inequality’s direction.
040c97c655b4: Why is the derivative of eˣ still eˣ? Real exponentiation introduced through e=lim(1+1/n)ⁿ satisfies lim(h→0)(eʰ−1)/h=1. We introduce this limit as a foundational fact here. Combined with the exponent addition rule, it gives the derivative used below.
eb1babc645a0: D · Mean, variance, and covariance: shape through average products
d607b64f3678: The mean is the total divided by the count. Variance averages squared deviations from the mean, not distances themselves. E denotes expectation; initially, think of it as an average over many samples. Cov denotes covariance. We describe a distribution using denominator N; the N−1 in unbiased sample estimation is a separate issue.
514e2192c27b: Samples (1,2) and (3,6) have mean (2,4). Their offsets are (−1,−2) and (1,2), producing identical outer-product tables:
e5b7c5c98e26: Diagonal entries give axis variances; off-diagonal entries indicate whether two coordinates tend to increase together. These two samples are collinear, so their matrix is singular. GS constructs a full ellipsoid from three positive scales and a rotation. “Positive definite” means positive variance in every nonzero direction.
ea7413a36a8b: E · Derivatives and partial derivatives: start with a two-point slope
02a67b387a19: A car travels Δdistance in Δtime; their ratio is average velocity. Shrinking interval h gives an instantaneous rate of change, written df/dx. We do not set h=0 and divide by zero; we examine the ratio as h approaches zero.
01d99a525883: A partial derivative ∂ holds all other inputs fixed and changes just one. With multiple outputs, arrange each output’s derivative with respect to each input in a table called the Jacobian. For one scalar output, the column of partial derivatives is its gradient ∇.
788e0e7f0477: The product rule follows by expanding (f+Δf)(g+Δg): after division by h, ΔfΔg/h tends to zero. Apply it to g·(1/g)=1 to derive the reciprocal rule, then combine the rules to obtain the quotient rule:
91d51c0f8453: F · Chain rule, backpropagation, and one update
4e7c077d6fe6: An input increase of 0.01 raises an intermediate value by about 0.03. Each unit increase in that intermediate value raises the output by about 5. The total change is 3×5×0.01. This is the chain rule: multiply along each path and add across paths.
8ed89f728fce: “Backward” sends slopes from the final error toward the inputs. If a value is used twice, add both paths’ contributions. A positive gradient means decreasing the parameter reduces error for a sufficiently small step:
fb28ba17b29e: η is the learning rate. PyTorch backward calculates gradients; optimizer.step changes parameters. This example uses SGD. The project’s teaching trainer uses Adam, with historical averages and adaptive steps, so its update equation differs.
8a1f8aca82fa: G · Completing the square and finding roots: algebra shared by ellipses and conditional Gaussians
ab18aca64652: Absorbing a linear term into a square is called completing the square. Expand the right-hand side to verify it. We later use the same idea to remove space–time cross terms.
d41931f49226: To solve λ²−sλ+p=0, move the constant to the right, add (s/2)² on both sides, and take square roots. Remember both positive and negative branches.
6ab4fd42741e: The matrix version also follows by multiplying out each term. Bold symbols need not stop a hand calculation: a 2×2 inverse only requires solving two pairs of linear equations.
0922ac5c0c3e: H · Integrals and the sphere: adding many small pieces
b33223c503d9: Distance can be approximated by summing many small velocity×time segments. As they become arbitrarily fine, the sum’s limit is an integral. The ds beside the integral identifies each piece’s width; keep track of its units.
9fd1faff6017: Spherical harmonics use the unit sphere. A direction v=(x,y,z) satisfies x²+y²+z²=1. Sines and cosines of angular coordinates can be understood through points on a unit circle. A spherical average weights small surface areas. Integrating sinθ·dθ·dφ gives the unit sphere’s area, 4π.
a1e85dd8de39: The final integral uses the fact that the derivative of cos is −sin: the inner integral is [−cosθ] from 0 to π, giving 2. Full trigonometric theory need not block your first GS implementation. Understand direction, evaluate the basis functions, and you can begin summing color.
244da3fcfcdc: Space uses 3D column vectors; time is a separate scalar. Understand the shared projection and composition first, then choose a dynamic representation.
